name: 1Password Events
description: Activity feed of a 1Password Business account from the 1Password Events API: sign-in attempts with outcome, client and location, item usage events (fill, reveal, copy, export, share) and audit events for user, vault, group and permission changes. Read-only; it never returns secret values.
instructions:
## 1Password Events API
This connector reads the **1Password Events API** (`https://events.1password.com` and the other regional hosts), the activity feed of a 1Password Business account that SIEM tools use: sign-in attempts, item usage events and audit events. It is read-only: the three list endpoints are POST requests only because the paging cursor travels in the body; nothing in 1Password changes.

**No secrets in this feed**: the events name users, vaults and items by uuid, with user names, emails, IP addresses and locations, but never return passwords or other item values. To read vaults and items use the separate 1Password Connect connector.

**Setup (about 5 minutes, owner or administrator of a 1Password Business account)**
1. Sign in on 1Password.com and open **Integrations** (then **Directory** if other integrations exist).
2. Under **Events Reporting** choose your SIEM, or **Other**, name the integration and select **Add Integration**.
3. Set up a bearer token: a name, an optional expiry (30, 90 or 180 days; default never) and the **Events to Report** (sign-in attempts, item usages, audit events). Select **Issue Token** and save it in 1Password.
4. Paste the token into `ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_TOKEN` and set `ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_URL` to the events host of the region your account is on: `https://events.1password.com` (1password.com), `https://events.ent.1password.com` (ent.1password.com), `https://events.1password.ca` (1password.ca) or `https://events.1password.eu` (1password.eu).
5. Install. `onepassword_events_introspect` checks the token.

**Workflow**
- Start with `onepassword_events_introspect`: `features` lists what the token may read. A list tool for a feature the token lacks answers 401.
- Suspicious logins, failed MFA, blocked countries: `onepassword_events_list_signin_attempts` for a time window.
- Who used or revealed an item, which integration fetched it: `onepassword_events_list_item_usages`, then match `item_uuid` and `vault_uuid`.
- Account changes (users invited, suspended or removed, vault permissions granted or revoked, groups, devices, service accounts and their tokens, exports): `onepassword_events_list_audit_events`.

**Paging**: the first call takes `start_time`, `end_time` (RFC 3339) and `limit` (1 to 1000, default 100); without times it returns the last hour. Every answer carries a `cursor` and `has_more`. While `has_more` is true, call the same tool again with only `cursor`. A cursor stays valid across sessions, so it can also be kept to fetch only newer events later. To change the window or page size, start again without a cursor.

**Reading the answers**: `items` holds the events, oldest first. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. Ids are 26-character uuids (`ETWZJTQCSRFPVOX74KERGHPBTU`). `country` and `location.country` are ISO country codes. Audit `action` and `object_type` are short codes (`grant`, `revoke`, `uva` = user vault access, `gva` = group vault access, `sa` = service account, `satoken` = service account token). Item usage actions are only recorded by 1Password 8.4.0 or later apps.

**Limits**: 600 requests per minute and 30,000 per hour per token; 429 means wait for the window to reset.

**Errors**: 401 with `{"Error":{"Message":"Unauthorized"}}` means a wrong, revoked or expired token, the wrong regional host, or a feature the token was not issued for. 400 means a malformed time or limit. 500: retry after a short wait and check https://status.1password.com.
prerequisites: A 1Password Business account and an owner or administrator who can set up an Events Reporting integration and issue its bearer token.

ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_URL.label: Events API host
ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_URL.help: The events host of your account's region: https://events.1password.com (1password.com), https://events.ent.1password.com (ent.1password.com), https://events.1password.ca (1password.ca) or https://events.1password.eu (1password.eu).
ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_URL.patternMessage: Use one of https://events.1password.com, https://events.ent.1password.com, https://events.1password.ca or https://events.1password.eu, without a trailing slash.

ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_TOKEN.label: Events Reporting bearer token
ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_TOKEN.help: 1Password.com, Integrations, Events Reporting: the bearer token issued for the integration (a long JWT starting with eyJ). It reads only the event types chosen when it was issued.
ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_TOKEN.patternMessage: Paste the whole bearer token (it starts with eyJ and has two dots), without Bearer in front.

verifyHints.401: 1Password refused the bearer token. It may be wrong, revoked or expired, or ONEPASSWORD_EVENTS_URL points at another region than your account (events.1password.com, events.ent.1password.com, events.1password.ca, events.1password.eu).
verifyHints.429: The Events API allows 600 requests a minute and 30,000 an hour. Wait for the window to reset.

tools.name: onepassword_events_introspect
tools.description: Check the Events API bearer token: returns its uuid, issued_at, the account_uuid and the features it may read (auditevents, itemusages, signinattempts). Call it first to see which of the other three tools this token can use.

tools.name: onepassword_events_list_signin_attempts
tools.description: Sign-in attempts to the 1Password account, successful and failed, oldest first: who (target_user name, email, uuid), when, outcome (category: success, credentials_failed, mfa_failed, sso_failed, firewall_failed, ...; type: credentials_ok, mfa_ok, password_secret_bad, totp_bad, country_blocked, ...), client app and version, OS, IP address and location. Needs the signinattempts feature. Returns items, cursor and has_more. Read-only although it is a POST.

cursor.description: Continue from where the previous call stopped: the `cursor` of the last response. When you pass it, leave limit, start_time and end_time out: the cursor already carries them.

limit.description: Events per page on a first call, 1 to 1000 (default 100).

start_time.description: First call only: earliest event time, RFC 3339 (e.g. 2026-10-29T00:00:00Z). Default: one hour before end_time, or one hour ago.

end_time.description: First call only: latest event time, RFC 3339 (e.g. 2026-10-30T00:00:00Z). Default: now.

tools.name: onepassword_events_list_item_usages
tools.description: Item usage events: when a user filled, revealed, copied, exported, shared or edited an item, or an integration fetched, created or updated it (action: fill, reveal, secure-copy, export, share, enter-item-edit-mode, select-sso-provider, server-fetch, server-create, server-update, other). Each event names the item_uuid, vault_uuid, used_version, the user, client and location; it never contains the item's secret values. Needs the itemusages feature. Returns items, cursor and has_more. Read-only although it is a POST.

end_time.description: First call only: latest event time, RFC 3339 (e.g. 2026-10-30T00:00:00Z). Default: now.

tools.name: onepassword_events_list_audit_events
tools.description: Audit events for actions team members took in the account: action (create, update, delete, activate, suspend, reactive, join, leave, grant, revoke, role, export, share, purge, ...), object_type (user, vault, item, group, device, invite, sso, sa (service account), satoken, ...), the actor (actor_uuid, actor_details), the object and aux object, session (ip, device, login time) and location. Needs the auditevents feature. Returns items, cursor and has_more. Read-only although it is a POST.
